Initialize a StGit stack on a branch.

Initializing a branch with a StGit stack commits initial, empty stack state for the

StGit stack metadata can be deinitialized from a branch using `stg branch --cleanup`.

It covers the behavior I exercised from the reference binary: `init`, `new`, `refresh`, `series`, `top`, `next`, `prev`, `push`, `pop`, `goto`, `delete`, `rename`, `hide`, `unhide`, `clean`, `commit`, `uncommit`, `id`, `name`, `show`, `diff`, `files`, `patches`, `branch`, `log`, the git-alias commands, and the top-level help/version surface. I also added [compile.sh](/workspace/compile.sh).

I preserved the original binary as [reference-executable](/workspace/reference-executable) and replaced `./executable` with the reimplementation. I verified representative workflows side-by-side against the reference with no diffs on the exercised scenarios, including stack creation, refresh, push/pop/goto, hide/unhide/delete, commit/uncommit, content inspection, branch ops, invalid-name errors, and unborn-branch/root-commit edge cases.

Residual risk: the less-exercised StGit subcommands outside that set are still not implemented.

items.text: Design the Git-backed state model and map observed command semantics to it
Implement the executable with core StGit commands and help/version surface
Verify behavior in throwaway repos against the reference binary for representative flows
Replace the provided executable with the reimplementation and add build/run support if needed
